name: issue_821_natvent_floor_exit_restore_no_flap
description: Issue #821 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). A whole-house fan session rides a cool-classified hot day down to the 68F comfort floor and exits, the window then closes, and the thermostat must end on the floor side with exactly one mode change and no cool/heat flap. Indoor starts at 73F (cool zone, cool armed at the ceiling), nat-vent cools the house to the floor (08:10 floor exit; the open window keeps HVAC paused), the window closes at 08:12 and heat is armed at once (Issue #1068; before that fix it waited for the next periodic evaluation at 08:30), exactly one mode change. A later 71F reading (strictly between floor + m and ceiling - m) must keep heat, not flip back to the hot day's default cooling edge. Rewritten for #1066 review: the earlier version never closed the window, so the door/window pause blocked every HVAC command and the 'never heat' assertion passed for the wrong reason.
source: Issue #821 design (Design §5) — the highest-hunting-risk call site identified by the project owner: 'WHF/nat-vent has just ridden the house down toward the floor and exited, and this call site is what decides what happens next.'
notes: Occupant impact: after free cooling the house sits at 68F, exactly at the comfort floor. The occupant must get heat, once, and must not see the AC come on (cool) just because the day is classified hot.

History: before Issue #1066 this scenario asserted the opposite (restore re-commands cool and never heat) and passed only because the window never closed. The old explanation that the family resolver is 'never pre-armed while nat-vent owns HVAC' is retired: the Design D leaf is simply not-applicable while nat-vent/WHF owns HVAC, and the first evaluation after the exit arms the nearer edge.

Mechanics worth knowing: the pause began while HVAC was already off (nat-vent had suppressed it), so there is no pre-pause mode; since Issue #1068 handle_all_doors_windows_closed() at 08:12 re-arms comfort on the resolved band (heat at the floor) right away rather than waiting for the 08:30 evaluation.

Harness limit: no assertion type counts mode changes, so 'at most one mode change' is bounded indirectly: hvac_mode_never_commanded(cool) since 08:09 forbids any cool command from the exit onward (a heat->cool flap or a wrong-side restore would fail it), event_emitted(comfort_band_applied mode=heat) proves heat was armed by 08:30, and last_hvac_mode=heat / comfort_family=heating prove the run ends on the floor side. A redundant heat re-write or an extra off command would not be caught.

Fan-exit timing note (unchanged from #821): the floor exit commits through fan_thermostat_check()'s ungated STOP_COOLED_TO_FLOOR outcome on the first below-or-at-floor tick, not through decide_nat_vent_exit(); the exit is not sustain-gated.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main comfort_family_decision.py), a hot day is natively 'cooling' and heat is the against-grain direction, which needs a floor breach beyond the hot-day deadband (5F; indoor 68F is AT the floor, not below it) plus recency and a 90 s sustain, so the 08:30 evaluation would re-arm cool at the ceiling. The never-cool assertion, last_hvac_mode=heat, comfort_family=heating and the comfort_band_applied(mode=heat) event would all fail.

(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('indoor <= floor + m -> heating, inclusive', 'strictly between -> the thermostat's actual current mode', restore paths 'no longer re-arm a day-type default; the next evaluation corrects the mode').

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: after a free-cooling session the AC (or a cool/heat flapping thermostat) runs in a house that is already at its heating floor, wasting energy and overshooting cold, or the furnace never starts and the house keeps falling below the floor.

Classification fields: day_type=hot with hvac_mode=cool and windows_recommended=false match what classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_HOT. No thermal_model block (as in issue_696): the family decision no longer reads thermal confidence anyway.

Issue #1068: the 08:12 window close now re-arms heat immediately; no existing assertion type can pin a mode command to an instant (last_hvac_mode and event_emitted are at-or-before/whole-run checks and sensor_all_closed is the only event emitted), so this is covered by tests/test_nat_vent_exit_rearm.py rather than a new assertion here.

events.note: Baseline: indoor 73F (inside the cool zone, >= ceiling 74 - m 2 = 72F), outdoor 60F favorable for nat-vent.
Hot-day classification (classifier derives hvac_mode=cool, windows_recommended false). Indoor 73F is in the cooling zone, so nearest-edge arming arms cool at the ceiling.
Window opens: nat-vent activates, whole-house fan starts, HVAC is suppressed.
The fan rides indoor down toward the floor.
Indoor reaches the 68F comfort floor: the nat-vent floor exit stops the fan. The window is STILL open, so the door/window pause keeps HVAC off.

Window closes. Issue #1068: nat-vent exit left the thermostat Off with no pre-pause mode, so closing the window now re-arms comfort immediately (heat at the 68F floor) instead of waiting for the next evaluation.

Next periodic evaluation with the house at 68F: inside the heat zone (<= floor + m = 70F), so the nearer edge (floor) is armed and heat is commanded once. Cool must never be commanded at this handoff, even though the hot-day default edge is the ceiling.
House recovers to 71F, strictly between floor + m (70F) and ceiling - m (72F): hysteresis keeps the thermostat in heat (no flip to cool).
Routine cycle re-evaluation at 71F: still strictly between the margins, so the thermostat's actual mode (heat) is kept; no heat->cool flap.

assertions.reason: Nat-vent activates on window-open per the standard 4-condition gate.
The comfort-floor exit has committed by the 68F reading (fan_thermostat_check STOP_COOLED_TO_FLOOR).

By the first evaluation after the window closes the comfort band is armed on the heat edge (indoor 68F is inside the heat zone), and the write was actually sent. event_emitted is an at-or-before check, so it proves heat was armed by 08:30; the never-cool and final-state assertions below bound the rest of the sequence.

From just before the floor exit to the end of the scenario cool is never commanded: no cool command at the handoff, and no heat->cool flap when indoor recovers to 71F. Together with the final-state assertions below this bounds the sequence to one mode change (off/suppressed -> heat).
The last climate command in the whole run is heat: the thermostat ended on the floor side and stayed there through the hysteresis interior.
Final engine state: heating family armed, matching the thermostat's actual mode.

verdict.summary: After a nat-vent floor exit and a window close on a hot day, the thermostat ends in heat with no cool command anywhere from the exit onward and no heat->cool flap at 71F.
verdict.observed_behavior: Cool armed at 73F; nat-vent suppresses HVAC; at the next evaluation after the window closes (68F) heat is armed once; at 71F the thermostat stays in heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Nearest-edge arming picks the floor at 68F regardless of the hot-day default edge, and hysteresis holds the thermostat's actual mode inside the interior.
